Bug_Title: Repeated patterns in regular expressions should not match the empty string
Bug_Details:
A regex should never include a repetitive pattern whose body would match the empty string. This is usually a sign that a part of the regex is
redundant or does not do what the author intended.
Noncompliant code example
"(?:)*"      // same as the empty regex, the '*' accomplishes nothing
"(?:|x)*"    // same as the empty regex, the alternative has no effect
"(?:x|)*"    // same as 'x*', the empty alternative has no effect
"(?:x*|y*)*" // same as 'x*', the first alternative would always match, y* is never tried
"(?:x?)*"    // same as 'x*'
"(?:x?)+"    // same as 'x*'
Compliant solution
"x*"
Bug_Explanation: The regular expression pattern includes a repeated pattern that would match the empty string. This does not accomplish anything and is redundant. The regular expression '(?:)+' is the same as an empty regex, and the '+' operator makes it match one or more occurrences of the empty pattern.
